newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-CHIEFS AGREE TO TERMS WITH ELVIS GRBAC.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-CHIEFS AGREE TO TERMS WITH ELVIS GRBAC.

text.p: The Kansas City Chiefs said Friday they had agreed in principle on a contract with free-agent quarterback Elvis Grbac.
In a statement, the team promised to release further details "when they become available."
According to published reports, the Chiefs had been negotiating with Grbac since their unsuccessful courting last month of free agent Jeff George, who signed with Oakland.

Grbac, 26, is a backup who started nine games for the San Francisco 49ers over the last three years. He is 6-3 as a starter with the Niners after compiling a 30-5-3 mark at the University of Michigan.
Grbac completed 62.2 percent of his passes last season for 1,236 yards with eight touchdowns and 10 interceptions.
Grbac's signing would continue the trend of 49er quarterbacks moving to Kansas City.
Joe Montana played the last two years of his legendary career with the Chiefs after winning four Super Bowls with San Francisco.
Steve Bono was acquired by Kansas City from the Niners in a May 1994 trade and again served as Montana's backup in his first season with the Chiefs.
After Montana retired, Bono became the starter in 1995, but was benched late in the 1996 season by coach Marty Schottenheimer in favour of backup Rich Gannon.

Kansas City flirted with George, who signed a five-year, $26 million deal with the Oakland Raiders. The Chiefs also expressed some interest in trading for Houston Oilers quarterback Chris Chandler, who eventually was dealt to Atlanta.
